Hey there!

We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Legal & Policy

As the legal team, we support all areas of Fever by offering scalable legal support – clear advice, risk management, and legal insight – that allow teams to move quickly and stay focused on what matters.

Our team is structured in:l Intellectual Property , Commercial, Strategic Transactions, Privacy, Dispute Resolution, and Legal Operations. Together, we cover the full legal landscape to meet the needs of a growing global business like Fever.

Join us if you are ready to tackle global challenges and provide strategic legal leadership to protect the long-term success of a rapidly growing tech leader.

We are looking for a driven and ambitious lawyer to join our international In-House Legal Team, supporting Fever’s fast-growing operations with primary responsibility for Brazil. Reporting directly to the Lead Counsel IBERIA, you will play a key role in enabling Fever’s continued regional expansion in Portugal and the rest of Iberia region.

As Legal Counsel - Portugal, you will provide proactive, business-oriented legal support across a wide range of matters — from commercial contracts and corporate governance to regulatory and compliance issues. You’ll collaborate closely with teams such as Business Development, Tax, Finance, Product, Originals and Operations to provide pragmatic, solution-oriented legal guidance that supports Fever’s continued growth across the region.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a diverse, high-performing legal team that combines strong technical expertise with a business-oriented mindset. You’ll work in a dynamic, international environment where your input will have real impact, contributing to Fever’s mission to democratize access to culture and entertainment experiences worldwide.

· Drafting / revising Portuguese and English language commercial contracts, terms and conditions, RFP submission documentation and similar legal documents

· Supporting commercial teams in the negotiation of deals and documents

· Researching legal issues related to product development and regulatory compliance

· Coordinating with internal stakeholders and external advisors to prioritise and manage legal matters

· Assisting and participating in knowledge management and operational excellence within Legal, including by identifying the need for and participating in preparation of templates, guides, processes and similar documents and tools

· Participating in ongoing compliance functions and product advice as required

· Upskilling, support, and growth of other team members

· Be a practising lawyer with 5+ years of post-qualification experience working in a Portuguese-speaking jurisdiction.

· Professional fluency in Portuguese and English is essential, with proficiency in an additional language a strong plus.

· Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a high level of emotional intelligence.

· Experience working on international projects or with global teams.

· A team player who is adaptable and eager to learn.

You can expect to join a team of diverse, hardworking, and kind professionals. We will strive to provide you with the tools and information needed to be successful in your role and grow professionally. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and invite them to demonstrate how they believe they can grow in this role.

This position will be located in Lisbon , with some flexibility for starting dates.

· Fever 40% discount: This discount is for personal use only.

· Free Candlelight Event: This voucher is for single use only and valid for 2 people.

· We offer private health insurance, managed by UNA. This is paid 100% by Fever.

· Meal tickets (Edenred): We have meal tickets worth 7.63 € per day, tax exempt.

· Wellhub Membership: Wellhub gives employees unlimited access to a selected number of gyms, studios, classes, training, and wellness apps. It is paid by Fever up to the Silver plan.

· English and Spanish Lessons fully paid by Fever.

· 22 working days of vacation per year.

· You can enjoy the afternoon off on your birthday if it falls on a working day. It’s our way of helping you celebrate!

· Free food and drinks in our kitchen.

· Home office friendly!

アイデンティティセキュリティ基盤「Josys」について
Josysは、企業内のあらゆる認証情報（アイデンティティ）を統合的に管理・防御する、AI駆動のアイデンティティセキュリティ基盤です。従業員・業務委託先のアカウントに加え、AIエージェントやサービスアカウントなど、人・AI・システムを横断して増加する認証情報を一元的に可視化し、守ります。
ダークウェブ起点の認証情報漏洩・感染端末の検知、AIエージェントの自動発見と管理、ポリシーにもとづくAIの自律型セキュリティ対応を中核に、SaaS統合管理で培ったアクセスガバナンスやライセンス最適化の機能を統合。権限管理やリスク対応を自動化し、セキュリティ人材不足のなかでも運用負荷を抑えながら、組織全体のアイデンティティを守ります。
Josysは、"すべてのアイデンティティ、すべてのアプリケーションを、AIで守る"ことを通じて、日本企業が安心して事業活動を行える環境づくりを推進してまいります。
解決する課題
急速に利用が拡大するSaaS・AIアプリにより、世界中のコーポレート部門は複雑な管理業務を求められる状況にあります。また、昨今のサイバーセキュリティインシデントでは、漏洩したIDを用いた攻撃がスタンダードとなっており、エンタープライズを中心により高いレベルでの対策が急務となっています。
一方で、求められる速度に管理が追いつかず、管理の抜け・更新漏れ・管理主体の分散など、企業のITガバナンスは危機的な状況にあります。これはコロナ禍を経てSaaS利用が増大した背景があり、日本だけでなくグローバルで同時多発的に発生している新しい課題であり、企業規模に関わらず多くの企業が抱えている経営リスクです。
そこで求められるのは、AIによってアイデンティティ・SaaS・デバイスの情報を統合的に管理し、リスクを最小化しながら運用を効率化することです。ジョーシスはAI Drivenなマネジメントプラットフォームを通じて、現場のオペレーションまで一貫して支援し、企業のアイデンティティ管理におけるガバナンス向上とセキュリティリスクの最小化に寄与します。
日本発グローバル企業への挑戦
海外発SaaSを国内で使う機会は多いものの、グローバルで使われる日本発SaaSはほとんどないのが実情です。それだけ "グローバルプロダクト" を事業として成功させることの難易度は高いとも言えます。JOSYSはそんな現状を打ち破り、日本をマザーマーケットとしながら世界でも使われるサービスを提供していくチャレンジの真っ只中にいます。この難易度の高い課題を、優秀なグローバルの同僚と共に、自分自身の手で創り上げていく熱い想いのある方を募集しています。
概要
本ポジションは、当社の日本国内およびグローバルにおける法務基盤・リーガルオペレーションをゼロから設計・推進する責任者候補のポジションです。 単なる契約書の審査にとどまらず、LegalOnなどのリーガルテックをフルに活用した業務の仕組み化・自動化の推進、グローバルガバナンス（GDPR、各国のプライバシー法対応）、および知的財産戦略の立案・実行まで、経営および各事業部門（営業・プロダクト・コーポレート等）のビジネスパートナーとして幅広く管轄していただきます。
業務内容
契約法務およびリーガルアドバイザリーの主導
各事業部門（NDA、業務委託、各種取引契約など）の契約審査・起草、およびビジネスのスピードを損なわない迅速なリスクアドバイスの提供
社内ステークホルダーに対する迅速かつ的確な法務相談窓口としての機能確立
リーガルオペレーション（テクノロジーの導入・定着）の推進
LegalOnを活用した契約審査体制の構築、およびAIレビュー精度向上のためのナレッジ蓄積・仕組み化
Slackなどのコミュニケーションツールと連携した、モダンな新・法務相談ワークフローの設計、全社展開、マニュアル作成

s.h: 社内メンバーや他部門へのITツール利用プロモーション、およびリーガルマインドの啓発
s.t:
法務プロセスの標準化・データベース化
契約書テンプレート（雛形）の継続的なアップデート、および過去の審査知見・過去事例のデータベース化
属人化しがちな法務タスクを可視化し、ITツール（DocuSign、Slack等）を用いた自動化施策の企画・実行
グローバルガバナンス＆海外子会社管理
グローバル拠点における法務リスクの把握、およびグループ全体に最適化されたガバナンス体制の構築
国内外の法規制変化（IT/SaaS関連領域含む）に対する継続的なモニタリングと、グループ全体への対応支援

s.h: 知的財産（IP）管理および戦略立案
s.t:
主要国における特許、商標、意匠権の取得戦略の立案、および権利化手続のプロセス管理
知的財産ポートフォリオの維持・管理、および侵害調査・トラブル対応
個人情報保護・プライバシー関連法務の構築

s.h: GDPR、日本の個人情報保護法、および関連する各国法令を順守するための体制（コンプライアンスフレームワーク）の構築・運用
s.t:
EU・UK Representative（EDPO等）をはじめとする外部機関・パートナーとの連携、およびクロスボーダーでのプライバシーガバナンス対応
求める経験

実務経験： 企業法務における契約審査・起草およびリーガルアドバイザリーの実務経験（目安：5年以上、またはそれに準ずる深い経験）
IT・AIへの高いリテラシー： 法務におけるテクノロジー活用（LegalOn、DocuSign、Slack、その他SaaSツール）に強い関心があり、既存のやり方に囚われず「より効率的な方法がないか」を自ら探求・実験することを楽しめるマインドセット
高いコミュニケーション・推進力： 変化の早いスタートアップ環境において、他部門（営業、プロダクト、経営管理など）の多様なステークホルダーと円滑に連携し、物事を前に進められるスキル

s.h: 法務部門における業務改善、BPR（ビジネスプロセス・リエンジニアリング）、またはITシステム/リーガルテック導入を主導した経験
s.t:
海外事業所の管理、国際法務におけるガバナンス構築、またはクロスボーダー案件におけるリスクマネジメントの実務経験
弁護士資格（日本または海外）をお持ちの方、あるいは法科大学院（ロースクール）修了と同等の法的バックグラウンド
求める人物像
「法務は守りだけでなく、ビジネスを加速させる機能である」という考え方に強く共感し、事業の成長にリーガル面からコミットしたい方
カオスな環境や新しいテクノロジー（生成AIや最先端のSaaS）をポジティブに捉え、自ら率先して手を動かしながら業務の仕組み化・自動化を楽しめる方
組織の成長フェーズに合わせて、柔軟に役割やスコープを拡張していける柔軟性のある方
ジョーシス掲載メディア

s.h: [日本経済新聞] ジョーシス、AIで不正アクセス検知 ID管理から防衛へ
s.t:
[IT Leaders] ジョーシス、SaaS/ID管理から「アイデンティティセキュリティ基盤」へ進化、AIで不正アクセスや過剰権限を自律対処

Satispay began by rethinking the simple act of a payment to remove the friction from our daily routines. But we didn't stop there. Today, we are building a complete financial platform designed to empower people and concretely improve their lives.
By giving our 6 million users a clear, open path to pay, save, and invest, we are evolving into the definitive destination for every financial need.
What you'll be doing
As our Legal Product Counsel, you’ll be the dedicated legal partner to our Product, Tech, and Design teams, embedding legal strategy directly into the product development lifecycle - from initial ideation to international launch. Here's what your day-to-day will look like:
End-to-End Product Counseling - Act as the primary legal architect for new products and features. You will also be embedded in the Product Team and proactively support the design phase to help Product Managers building up innovative and exciting new services and features that delight our customers.
Regulatory Navigation - Analyze complex financial and consumer protection regulations across European jurisdictions, translating legal requirements in product and design guidance.
Cross-Functional Collaboration - Partner closely with Product, Tech, Strategy, Marketing, Operations and Compliance teams to balance business objectives with smart risk management.
Consumer Law - Provide advice on financial, consumer protection laws and legal issues related to the B2C and B2B expansion of the Satispay ecosystem.

We need a problem-solver who loves teamwork and gets things done. If you're curious and ready for real ownership, you'll fit in! Does this sound like you?
Background & Experience - At least 5 years of experience as Product Counsel advising on technology products, commercial, and consumer law issues. Significant in-house experience within a fast-growing Tech or Fintech company is highly preferred.
Fintech & Product DNA - Deep familiarity with the fintech ecosystem (e.g., APIs, payment schemes, card networks, wallet architectures, open banking) and the regulatory complexities of scaling digital financial products across Europe.
Product Curiosity - A genuine passion for UX/UI, technology, and understanding how a product works under the hood. You enjoy bridging the gap between engineering logic and legal frameworks.
Strategic Risk-Taking - Ability to make decisions in ambiguous, fast-paced environments. You provide risk-adjusted recommendations, not just a list of legal restrictions.
Communication & Influence - Exceptional communication skills with the ability to distill dense legal concepts into clear, actionable advice for product managers, engineers, and executives.
Language Proficiency - Full professional fluency in English. Experience working in international environments or advising on cross-border European rollouts is a major asset.

s.t:
We move fast, and evolution never stops. It's a fun ride, but it can be challenging. To make sure our people truly thrive, we're committed to making their lives easier, both in the office and out in the world. That's why we created CareAbout:
❤️ Health (Private insurance for you and your family, psychological support with Serenis, mental health workshops)
💰 Financial resources (Stock Option Plan, Meal vouchers, Relocation support if you’re moving countries)
⚙️ Growth and development (Professional development programs, Internal mobility, Language courses with Preply)
🌱 Flexibility (Unlimited PTO, Hybrid working policy*, Flexible working hours)
👨‍👩‍👧 Family (Enhanced parental leave, Additional leave for child sickness)
*We embrace three days per week in-office (Tuesday and Thursday + 1 of your choice), with the option to request extra remote time.

s.h: Initial salary: Starting from €58,000 gross per annum
s.t:

The final compensation package is tailored according to your unique experience and expertise. If your skills go beyond the standard profile, apply anyway so we can discuss a package that reflects your true value.

What you'll be doing
As our Corporate Governance Counsel, you’ll be the person who connects the dots between corporate structure, regulatory expectations, and business strategy to shape the future of Satispay's governance.

s.h: Here's what your day-to-day will look like
s.t:
Regulatory Governance (Circular CSSF 26/906) — Lead the legal implementation of the regulatory framework on internal governance and central administration, ensuring governance arrangements between the Supervisory and Management Bodies are robust and transparent.
Corporate Administration & Substance — Support the relevant corporate bodies to ensure that decision-making processes and administrative centers are legally sound and compliant with the latest regulatory expectations.
Board & Committee Management — Direct the legal management of the Board of Directors, relevant committees, and Shareholders' meetings, drafting complex minutes and resolutions.
Corporate Legal Strategy — Proactively identify governance upgrades needed as we scale and advise on organizational design from a governance/regulatory lens.

We need a problem-solver who loves teamwork and gets things done. If you're curious and ready for real ownership, you'll fit in! Does this sound like you?
Background — You are a lawyer with 7 to 10 years of experience built in top-tier Luxembourg or international law firms, ideally complemented by significant in-house experience in regulated Fintech, Banking, or Insurance companies.
Luxembourg Regulatory Mastery — You possess a deep understanding of the Luxembourg regulatory landscape.
Governance Expertise — You have a proven track record in managing complex corporate governance structures.
Strategic & Risk-Based Approach — You can balance strict regulatory requirements with business agility, providing out-of-the-box legal solutions that manage risk effectively.
Communication & Influence — You are confident in advising senior management, the Board of Directors, and external stakeholders with clarity and professional judgment.
Language Proficiency — You are fluent in English. Knowledge of French and Italian is considered a plus.

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
Wayflyer moves fast and the legal infrastructure that supports how we fund ourselves and serve our merchants has to move with it. We need a finance lawyer who can hold the complexity of our debt facilities and lending products in one hand, and the needs of our commercial teams in the other. This isn't a role for someone who wants to sit behind a wall of disclaimers. It's for someone who wants to be in the room where decisions get made.
What you'll actually do
You'll be the primary legal voice on everything touching our external funding, implementing and maintaining debt facilities, working through intercreditor arrangements, and making sure our capital markets activity is properly supported end to end.
You'll work alongside our business teams on our core lending and merchant cash advance products, fielding queries from across our geographies and making sure the answers are actually useful to the people asking them.
You'll own our contractual templates and playbook, keeping them current, making them sharper, and rebuilding them when the business has grown past what they were designed for.
When we're launching new products or enhancing existing ones, you'll be the person stress-testing the legal side before we go live. And you'll manage local counsel across jurisdictions, which means knowing when to delegate, when to push back, and when to roll up your sleeves.
What this role could turn into
Finance lawyers at Wayflyer don't stay narrowly defined for long. This role has a natural path toward leading the legal function for a specific product vertical, or stepping up into a broader General Counsel track as we scale. There's also a real opportunity to shape how we use AI and legal tech across the team, if you're genuinely curious about that space, you'll have room to lead on it.
Who thrives here
You're the kind of lawyer who gives advice people can actually act on. You translate complexity without losing the nuance that matters, and you know the difference between managing risk and just saying no. You don't wait to be asked, if you spot a gap in a template or a problem in a process, you fix it. You're comfortable with ambiguity and pace, and you've learned that the best legal work often happens outside the strict boundaries of the brief you were given.
We hire for range
You're a qualified solicitor with around 4-6 years' PQE in banking and finance, whether from a leading firm or a comparable in-house environment. You have solid experience across facility documentation, security structuring, and cross-border financing. What matters more than where you've been, though, is how you work: commercially minded, transactionally confident, and genuinely interested in what happens when legal meets product.
Location and working policy
📍 This role is based in our Dublin or London office, with a hybrid working policy.
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and a pension. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

This is Adyen

Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.

For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

Corporate Legal Counsel

As Corporate Legal Counsel within Corporate Legal’s Advisory team, you will primarily be working on matters relevant to Adyen’s public listing in the Netherlands. You will also help the team facilitate our major corporate projects such as, capital markets enquiries, complex corporate projects and corporate development.

This is a strategic role that is important to sound corporate governance practices and continued sustainable growth. The role requires someone effective at cross collaboration, who excels at decision making in a fast-moving complex environment. Knowledge of and comfort with the Market Abuse Regulation is imperative to success.

The counsel will drive discussions and decisioning on disclosure matters as well as advise on public filings and equity matters. The role forms part of Adyen’s larger corporate practice which covers corporate governance, litigation and disputes and corporate development.

The corporate legal team is currently centered in Amsterdam and the United States but Adyen is a global company with offices, entities, and boards all over the world.

· Review and advise on public filings as well as other disclosure documentation.

· Providing legal support and internal training on other corporate law matters as required, such as Mergers & Acquisitions, corporate development and other corporate legal initiatives.

· Manage insider trading and conflict of interest inquiries, procedures, and policies.

· Ensure compliance with the Market Abuse Regulation.

· Support the disclosure committee, driving strategic disclosure reviews and determinations.

· Partner with Investor Relations and Communications on disclosure matters.

Protect Democracy is seeking an experienced, highly motivated attorney to join our team as Senior Counsel, focusing on the legal dimensions of artificial intelligence and advanced technology as they intersect with American democracy.

This role is integral to our scaling of the AI for Democracy Action Lab — Protect Democracy ’s multidisciplinary, nonpartisan “action tank” focusing on building tech tools and shaping law and policy to safeguard and strengthen democracy in the AI era.

This position is remote based in the US.* Please note: We are no longer hiring early-mid career Tech Counsel.

This is a position for candidates with at least 10 years of experience as an attorney, ideally including expertise in AI and emerging technology law, exceptional legal and analytical skills, entrepreneurial legal instincts, and a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for diverse audiences.

In this role, you will develop and advance legal strategies at the frontier of AI law and policy. From idea generation to execution, you will work with a small team driving creative impact litigation and other projects that integrate legal, regulatory, and communications strategies to constrain deployments of AI that are corrosive to our democracy.

You will also help build the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s expertise and credibility on the legal questions that will define how AI shapes our democracy. As a member of this team, you will shape the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s legal advocacy priorities, building upon the team’s strategies to date.

Our legal work has included advocacy to push back against the Pentagon’s retaliation against Anthropic for standing by its red lines, litigation challenging the administration’s attempt to chill online trust and safety work, and litigation and advocacy to stop the administration’s unlawful collection and aggregation of Americans’ personal data and deployment of technology for surveillance purposes.

At Protect Democracy , we believe that diversity isn’t just a strength — it’s a necessity for tackling the complex challenges facing democracy. A broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthen our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change.

We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. If you meet most but not all of the criteria listed below but believe nonetheless you’d be a stellar match for the role and could grow into it, we want to hear from you.

In this role, you will: Identify, scope, and manage complex, high-stakes integrated advocacy projects to advance the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s goals; Lead and drive the development of innovative legal arguments and potential litigation approaches at the intersection of AI and democracy; Lead the process of researching, drafting, and editing pleadings, motions, briefs, and other legal filings in impact litigation; Lead communication with opposing counsel and manage and grow relationships with clients, coalition partners, experts, and government stakeholders in high-stakes litigation and non-litigation settings; Manage discovery processes, including informal fact-finding, document review, witness interviews, written discovery, depositions, and expert discovery; Supervise and mentor paralegals, junior legal staff, and law students; Write, publish, and present to key audiences on legal issues that gain significant traction at the intersection of AI and democratic governance; Brief reporters and provide expert commentary on complex legal questions and developments in AI law and regulation, serving as a public face for projects; Engage with policymakers, regulators, civil society partners, and the tech industry as a credible legal voice for pro-democracy AI governance.

Requirements The ideal candidate brings: At least 10 years of legal experience (which can include judicial clerkships), with expertise in AI and emerging technology law, exceptional legal and analytical skills, entrepreneurial legal instincts, and a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for diverse audiences; Bar membership in good standing in the jurisdiction of your residence; Experience developing and leading impact litigation or plaintiff-side civil litigation, including managing litigation teams for the senior role; Entrepreneurial legal instincts and an ability to generate impactful, creative ideas that advance the goals of the AI for Democracy Action Lab; Exceptional analytical, writing, and presentation skills directed at both legal and non-legal audiences; Ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for policymakers, journalists, and the public An embrace of a cross-ideological and nonpartisan approach to protecting our democracy; Growth mindset and enthusiasm for giving and receiving feedback up, down, and sideways; Collaborative orientation and willingness to take on tasks big or small as needed to advance our mission; Rigorous attention to detail and the highest standards for excellence in execution; A passionate commitment to the preservation of democratic norms and institutions, and an understanding that our democracy has never fully represented communities of color.

This position serves as a Senior Attorney Advisor in the Legal Programs Office of the Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA).

In coordination with EOUSA's Office of Legal Education and other Department components, identify training needs and advise on/oversee the development and delivery of training for the USAOs. Recommend appropriate changes to operations and policies to ensure adherence with applicable authorities and to promote program effectiveness.

Advocate for and represent the interest of USAOs on various Department and intra-agency working groups and committees as it relates to assigned program areas and Department priority initiatives.

Plan, execute, and coordinate a variety of innovative and high visibility pilot projects to facilitate and enhance the work of the USAOs and further the mission of the Department and EOUSA. Responsibilities will increase and assignments will become more complex as your training and experience progress.

· Frequently collaborate with cross-functional legal and business teams to practically balance legal risk with business needs and objectives.

· Identify opportunities for improving internal litigation processes and implement solutions.

· Strategize, coordinate, and manage all aspects of pre-litigation matters.

· 4+ years of litigation experience; a plus factor would be in-house experience and/or experience in the technology or gaming industries.

· Intellectual curiosity and strategic, proactive decisionmaking.

· Interest in working in a fast-paced environment where no day is like another.

· Willingness to engage in new and unfamiliar tasks with minimal oversight.

· Ability to effectively prioritize and balance multiple tasks and responsibilities.

· Effective and direct communicator who is experienced and interested in working in a collaborative environment, partnering with both legal and business teams.

· Familiarity with the US litigation process (international experience a plus).

· Detail oriented and driven to provide high-quality work.

This position supports the work of DOE's Complex Fraud and Retail Fraud & General Enforcement Task Forces. The Task Forces are responsible for conducting investigations and enforcement activities pursuant to the Act and Regulations.

This includes investigating suspected violations, as well as carrying out civil actions in federal district courts such as injunctive proceedings, hearings, and trials. If selected, you will join a well-respected team, serving as a trial attorney, responsible for investigating suspected violations of and enforcing the Act and Regulations.

At the full performance level, the duties include: The incumbent plans, organizes, and participates in or directs investigations of suspected violations of the Act and Regulations. Such investigations may include issuing document requests, taking testimony under oath, and gathering and analyzing documents and trading records.

The incumbent supervises or independently interviews witnesses during the investigation. The incumbent supervises or independently assembles, correlates, studies, and analyzes the data obtained and prepares reports of facts developed, including detailed exhibits, schedules, and other documents.

The incumbent also briefs DOE management as to factual findings, legal analyses, and recommendations on how to proceed. The incumbent participates in the prosecution of civil actions in federal district courts on behalf of the CFTC.

This includes drafting complaints, motions, and other briefing; taking depositions; propounding and responding to discovery requests; and representing the CFTC in hearings and trials. The incumbent participates in the administrative resolution of enforcement matters.

This includes drafting proposed administrative orders for the CFTC's consideration, as well as drafting corresponding offers and CFTC memoranda recommending specific resolutions.

Serves as the lead or junior attorney in cases, coordinating and supervising the work activities of other assigned staff in conducting investigations and preparing for and conducting trials before federal district courts. Participates in and assists in formal training activities of DOE staff within its various offices.

As directed by the assigned supervisor, the incumbent conducts liaison activities with the Department of Justice/U.S. Attorney's Offices and other law enforcement and regulatory authorities, such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S.

Postal Inspection Service, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and State Attorneys General, among others, regarding enforcement activities, including the investigation and prosecution of fraud cases.

Recommends to the assigned supervisor, when appropriate, that evidence obtained during an investigation indicating that criminal violations of the federal commodity laws have occurred, be referred to the Department of Justice.

Matters or other projects assigned to the incumbent for investigation and litigation involve complex legal or factual issues (or both). Such difficulties most frequently arise from the factual and legal complexity of the matter under investigation/litigation.

Matters are frequently of such a nature that their outcome will have a significant effect on the commodity derivatives industry or a major segment thereof. Because of the importance of the matters assigned, the incumbent can be expected to face capable and qualified legal counsel throughout the duration of the open matter.
BASIC REQUIREMENT: All applicants must possess the following: J.D.; and Active membership of the bar in good standing in any state, territory of the United States, the District of Columbia, or the commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

(Note: proof of bar membership will be required before entry on duty) AND To qualify at each grade level, you must have the following: CT-13: You must have a J.D. and/or LLM equivalent Degree, bar membership and three years of relevant legal practice experience, acquired after being admitted to the bar, commensurate with the duties and responsibilities of a legal position.

Relevant experience is defined as an attorney, law clerk, or other legal experience which was obtained subsequent to graduation from law school.

Qualifying experience may include: demonstrating excellent writing and critical thinking skills; participating in investigations; interviewing witnesses; researching and writing legal memoranda and litigation documents; knowledge of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and Federal Rules of Evidence; developing case strategy; engaging in all aspects of discovery, including depositions; and assisting attorneys in preparation for and participating in trials.

CT-14: You must have a J.D. and/or LLM equivalent Degree, bar membership and four years of relevant of legal practice experience, acquired after being admitted to the bar, commensurate with the duties and responsibilities of a legal position.

Relevant experience is defined as an attorney, law clerk, or other legal experience which was obtained subsequent to graduation from law school.

Qualifying experience may include: demonstrating excellent writing and critical thinking skills; leading investigations; taking primary responsibility in interviewing witnesses; researching and writing legal memoranda and litigation documents; substantial knowledge of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and Federal Rules of Evidence; developing case strategy; engaging in and having primary responsibility for all aspects of discovery, including depositions; having primary responsibility in preparing for and conducting trials; briefing senior managers or clients on factual developments and legal theories of ongoing investigations and litigations.

Selections may be made at all grade levels.

Lyft is seeking a sharp, dynamic, and self-motivated attorney with at least 5 years litigation and counseling experience to achieve Lyft’s business goals at the intersection of law, policy, and technology.

You’ll serve as a trusted advisor to multiple internal business partners, and your work to minimize legal risk to the Company will be core to the success of the organization.

The successful candidate will be ethical, entrepreneurial and resourceful, skilled at building strong relationships, and comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. You will report directly to a Director on the Litigation team.

· Primary responsibility — meaning, hands-on work, not just supervising outside counsel — for a wide variety of litigation matters, pre-litigation dispute resolution, internal counseling, and other legal disputes, with an emphasis on consumer litigation, regulatory disputes, government investigations, and competition.

· Proactively approach all aspects of litigation, including discovery, motion practice, witness preparation, settlement negotiations, and trial and appellate strategies.

· Work closely with internal business partners to provide strategic and proactive legal advice on litigation and regulatory matters, including but not limited to understanding, interpreting, and applying current law and regulations to Lyft’s current and prospective products and services.

· Provide strategic recommendations to a broad range of cross-functional teams addressing regulatory and other matters.

· Provide legal guidance to departments such as Compliance, Public Policy, Communications, Customer Care, Product, Marketplace, and Lyft Urban Solutions to help craft solutions to the novel legal challenges Lyft faces every day.

· Manage outside counsel, including tactical guidance, staffing, case management, budgeting, and alignment with Lyft’s broader legal strategy.

· J.D. degree from a top-tier law school and active membership in at least one state bar.

· 5+ years civil litigation experience at a mid to large size law firm and/or a regulatory agency. Strong preference is given to candidates with prior in-house experience.

· Prior experience with regulatory disputes and government investigations, competition matters, and complex or consumer class actions is preferred.

· Excellent problem-solving capabilities, strategic thinking, judgment, communication, and interpersonal skills.

· Both detail oriented and able to see the big picture.

· Ability to operate autonomously while being a team player who brings a positive attitude to the workplace and is willing to jump on any project, big or small.

· Executive presence and ability to communicate legal risks and recommendations to senior leaders.

· Demonstrated ability to make decisions and influence through excellent verbal and written communication skills.

· Ability to think quickly on your feet and simultaneously manage workloads, multiple client demands and shifting priorities.

· Be a resourceful self-starter and have a passion for results. Embody Lyft’s culture, and operate with high standards and ethics

· An understanding of the multi-modal transportation and ridesharing industries, as well as the sharing economy in general.

· Passion for Lyft and the ridesharing community.

Ready to scale your career at the intersection of law and innovation? Join Okta’s Public Sector and Regulated Offerings Legal Team . As Corporate Counsel, you won’t just be reviewing regulatory requirements—you’ll be a foundational builder of a scalable, global Public Sector practice.

In this role, you will provide frontline legal counseling for Okta’s most critical regulated environments, working both independently and alongside senior leadership to navigate the complexities of the U.S. government’s regulatory frameworks.

You will partner with business and technology teams to guide the development and implementation of Okta’s Public Sector solutions. Our Public Sector legal team drives the legal strategy for introducing new products and features into regulated environments (e.g., FedRAMP, GovRAMP, DoD CC SRG).

In this role, you must use sharp critical thinking to provide pragmatic legal solutions that balance aggressive business objectives with necessary risk mitigation. Finally, you serve as a bridge between legal, engineering, compliance, security, and sales teams to ensure our products meet the rigorous standards of our public sector customers.
